findings.title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser record exists
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately calls `tu.notification_level`. A TopicUser row is only created when a user has viewed/tracked/posted in a topic, but the email unsubscribe link is sent to users who may have received a notification (e.g. via watch category or a mention) without ever having opened the topic. For those users find_by returns nil and `tu.notification_level` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of muting the topic. The code should use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)` which upserts the row.

findings.title: State-changing GET endpoint with no CSRF token or confirmation
findings.body: The unsubscribe action permanently changes the user's notification level (potentially to muted) as a side effect of a plain GET request, with no CSRF token and no confirmation step. Email scanners, link prefetchers (mail clients, antivirus, some browsers) follow links in emails; if the user's browser session is active or the link is fetched through a prefetching proxy that carries cookies, the topic can be muted without the user ever clicking. The rest of the codebase uses keyed, token-protected unsubscribe endpoints (see `email/unsubscribe/:key`); the per-topic link should either be tokened or the GET should only display a page where the change is made via a POST/XHR.

findings.title: Direct AR save bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
findings.body: unsubscribe mutates the TopicUser record directly with `tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!` instead of going through TopicUser.change. As a result `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are never updated (they should be set to user_changed), and no `notification_level_change` MessageBus message is published to `/topic/:id` for that user, so an open tab will keep showing the stale notification level. All other paths that change notification level in the app use TopicUser.change for these reasons.

findings.title: Toggle to 'regular' contradicts the 'stop receiving notifications' message
findings.body: When the user's level is tracking or watching, the action sets it to `regular`, not `muted`. But a regular user still receives notifications for direct replies and mentions. The email text ('To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here') and the client locale ('You will stop receiving notifications for...') promise that notifications stop, yet the user will continue to be emailed on replies. Either the action should always mute, or the copy must say notifications are reduced to direct replies only.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link locale now requires %{unsubscribe_url} for all callers
findings.body: The server locale `unsubscribe_link` was changed to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`, and MessageBuilder renders it whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true (both in html_part and body). Only UserNotifications#send_notification_email passes `unsubscribe_url`. Any other caller (plugins, or future core mailers) that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without supplying `unsubscribe_url` will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when building the email. Either the locale should tolerate a missing URL or the builder should default unsubscribe_url when absent.

findings.title: List-Unsubscribe header not updated to the per-topic URL
findings.body: MessageBuilder#header_args still sets the List-Unsubscribe header to `user_preferences_url` even when a topic-specific `unsubscribe_url` was supplied in the same opts. Mail clients that use the List-Unsubscribe one-click header will therefore send users to global preferences instead of the per-topic unsubscribe page, defeating the feature for those clients.

findings.title: No test that the per-topic unsubscribe URL appears in the email
findings.body: The spec was only updated to pass `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` so the existing assertions keep passing; there is no assertion that this URL actually appears in the body or html_part, and no controller or mailer spec for the new TopicsController#unsubscribe action (nil TopicUser case, redirect on slug mismatch, toggle semantics). The core behavior of this PR is untested.
